appStoreVersionLocalization.promotionalText: Run AI coding agents on your own Mac or Linux machine and keep up with them from iPhone and iPad: approve risky steps, answer questions, and review changes.
description: Oppi lets you run AI coding agents on your own Mac or Linux computer and follow them from iPhone and iPad. Start a task, step away, and Oppi tells you when an agent has a question or needs approval.

Oppi works with a server you run yourself. There is no Oppi account and no hosted session store. Your code stays on your computer, and the agent uses the AI model provider you connect, such as Anthropic or OpenAI. Agent commands, tools, and extensions run on your paired server, never on your iPhone or iPad.
Set up from your iPhone
Sign in to Tailscale in the app or enter any SSH host, pick your computer, and Oppi installs and starts its server there, then pairs. You can also install from a terminal and scan a QR code.
What you can do
• Watch agent sessions stream in a native timeline
• Answer questions and approve or deny risky commands, with optional Face ID
• Get notifications when an agent needs you or finishes, encrypted end to end
• Review changed files and diffs, and comment on lines
• Browse workspace files: code, Markdown, images, PDF, diagrams
• Attach photos and files, sketch, and annotate
• Dictate prompts on device or through your server
• Run several agents across workspaces and see which ones need you
• On iPad, and on the iPhone Duo's inner display, keep your sessions beside the chat and open files or Git in a side panel
Works with iOS
• Share extension: send text, links, photos, videos, and files from other apps to start a session
• Controls: start a new session from Control Center, the Lock Screen, or the Action Button
• Siri and Shortcuts: start a session or send a request to Oppi by voice or from a shortcut
• Live Activities: see on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island how many sessions are running or need you
• SSH terminal: open a shell on computers you add; it connects directly from your device
The agents run on your computer, using the open-source Pi coding agent. Oppi shows and controls them; it does not mirror your screen.
Privacy policy: https://github.com/duh17/oppi/blob/main/docs/privacy.md
Support: https://github.com/duh17/oppi/blob/main/docs/support.md

notes: Oppi is a native client for an Oppi server the user runs on their own Mac or Linux computer. No Oppi account; no desktop mirroring. "Pi" is the open-source MIT Pi coding agent by Mario Zechner (pi.dev) that the server runs.
REVIEWER PATH (the review server stands in for the user's computer)
1. Tap Set Up a Computer > Set Up a Mac or Linux Computer.
2. Computer: Other. Host <FILL: review host>, user reviewer, password <FILL: password>. Tap Check.
3. Confirm host key SHA256:<FILL: host key fingerprint>, tap Trust Key and Check, then Pair.
4. Open workspace "review", send "<FILL: prompt>", then Allow or Deny the approval.
Fallback: scan the attached pairing QR, valid until <FILL: QR expiry date>.
LIVE VOICE (hands-free voice conversation with the agent)
1. Settings > Experiments: turn on Live Voice (off by default).
2. In a session, touch and hold the composer's mic button, then choose Live Voice. Or say "Call Oppi" to Siri.
3. iOS shows its call screen. Speak; the agent answers aloud. End the call there or from the Lock Screen.

The review server has a voice service. Live Voice is an outgoing CallKit call, so audio continues while locked or in the background; that is the only use of voip. No incoming calls, PushKit, or Recents entries.
FEATURES
- Share sheet: text, URLs, images, and files start a session.
- Controls (Control Center, Lock Screen, Action Button): New Session, Live Voice.
- Siri/Shortcuts: "Start a session in Oppi" confirms prompt, workspace, and server first; "Ask Oppi" sends to a new session in the background; "Call Oppi" starts Live Voice.
- Live Activities (optional): two counts only, threads needing the user and threads running.
- iPad and iPhone Duo inner display, landscape: sessions sidebar beside the chat; files and Git open in a side column.
- SSH Terminal (Settings > SSH Hosts): connects from the device straight to hosts the user saves, after checking the host key.
- Tailscale: in-app sign-in runs a userspace node for Oppi's own connections; no VPN profile or Network Extension.
- Model Providers: API keys stay on the user's server; browser sign-in for providers built into Pi (Anthropic, OpenAI, GitHub Copilot, xAI, others).
- MCP Servers: OAuth sign-in from the phone; credentials stay on the server.
- Edit with Oppi: "Describe a change" on Agents, schedules, Skills, and workspaces starts a session that asks before applying it.
VISIBLE BUT NOT TESTABLE ON THE REVIEW SERVER
- Rex and Herdr (Server Settings > Features): Terminal integrations for the Rex and herdr terminal tools on the user's own computers. The review server has Rex turned off and runs neither.
- Durable Sessions (Server Settings, off by default): the server saves each turn so sessions resume after a server restart.
NOTES

- Agent commands, tools, extensions, and installers run on the user's paired server, never on iOS. The app downloads no code that changes its features. HTML previews run in a WKWebView with network blocked and no native bridge.

- No public content, other users, or third-party software catalog. Extensions and Skills are files on the user's server; the app shows their display-only output and exposes no native APIs. The model provider applies its own filtering.
- Third-party AI: before content first goes to a model or voice provider, the app names it and asks. Withdraw in Settings > Privacy & Security.
- Push is optional and end-to-end encrypted; our relay cannot read alerts. It needs App Attest; without it the app still works.
- audio background mode: Live Voice, and playback the user started (workspace media, voice replies).
- Microphone: server dictation and Live Voice send audio to the user's Oppi server and its speech or voice service.
- Face ID: App Lock, confirming new or changed servers, and protected actions such as removing a server or setting an API key.

pricing.$comment: Free. apply creates a free price schedule only when none exists and refuses to change a non-free one.

availability.$comment: Every territory except France (no French encryption declaration) and China mainland (CallKit is not allowed there).
